Intertextuality is a method, skill, or discipline and a guide for the scientific analysis of texts, especially artistic and non-artistic works, to determine the presence of influence through borrowing or dialogue; that is, the similarity in form, content, and technique between one text and another. This resemblance can be direct or involve proximity. Such interaction is also referred to as an echo. It is believed that intertextuality is among the oldest compositional techniques; however, as a critical approach, it still appears to be unfamiliar and has not been extensively addressed in the field of Kiswahili literature and art. For this reason, this article will contribute to the Kiswahili body of work dealing with criticism through the theory of intertextuality, in order to identify the intertextuality present in texts, for example in the play Our Cohesion Our Triumph. The results of the analysis have revealed a considerable presence of intertextuality connected to the author’s upbringing and development in religious (spiritual), physical (cultural and moral), social, and academic dimensions – in one way or another. It is part of these findings that constitutes this article. Therefore, this article presents the intertextuality between the selected play Our Cohesion Our Triumph and writings from sacred books, allegory in the selection and creation of characters, philosophical echoes, chapter or plot titles, and the mythology of symbols. The play employs language that is quickly and easily understood by anyone well-versed in Kiswahili. The dialogues constructed in this play evoke a variety of themes such as liberation, the role of women in society, social classes, sabotage, selfishness, intrigue, oppression, hatred, jealousy, greed, betrayal, exploitation, abuse, discrimination, transparency and truth, customs and traditions, unity and solidarity, family upbringing, effort and sustainable development, the importance of preserving records and identifying property, as well as the management and advancement of property, among others. What is important for the reader of this article to understand is that intertextuality cannot be identified in a text if the analyst lacks background knowledge or familiarity with the knowledge, techniques, skills, and traits found in various preceding texts. Therefore, a person who can identify intertextuality in artistic works must be a highly knowledgeable and inquisitive individual, someone with a thirst and hunger for knowledge, techniques, skills, and the characteristic curiosity gained through exploring various creative works and a range of academic writings. On the contrary, a reader will not be able to discern the intertextuality within the creative work they are reading if they do not mentally perceive the resonances of knowledge, techniques, skills, and traits found in earlier works. The play is rich in various artistic and theoretical experiments and techniques. For example, within the play, there is intertextuality as each chapter is given a subtopic that refers to linguistic terms from the field of structural linguistics, in order to illustrate the birth and development of the subject matter being discussed by the author. In this book, these scholars explain that, typically, the human brain has an area responsible for recording, storing, and rapidly retrieving memories of events and experiences a person has encountered. Therefore, when a reader comes across an event or technique that they have previously encountered in another work, their mind immediately responds and triggers a sensation that draws on the recall of that event or technique. The retrieval of a previous event, matter, or technique in relation to what has just been encountered produces an intersection of two texts. This intersection creates a resonance of the event, technique, or matter within the reader’s mind. All of these processes occur very rapidly. Therefore, you cannot recognize the presence of intertextuality if you are not a keen reader or a careful follower of different matters and various writings—both extensively and in depth. Allegory is an artistic device used by a writer to choose a name that reflects the character, behavior, and experiences of a character in the work they are creating. For example, a writer may name their character “Hasidi” (The Envious One). To justify this name, the writer must develop that character to act with envy from beginning to end. The selection and creation of characters whose traits align with their names is the artistic technique known as allegory. Normally, these characters possess the traits of flat characters (those who do not undergo changes in character) in order to justify their names, because if they were to change in character, their names would no longer correspond to their new traits. Therefore, in terms of character and stance, these characters remain unchanged from the beginning to the end of the play. Mlacha and Madumulla (1991) describe such characters as ones who do not appear to grow in character, actions, or psychologically. The main goal of this approach is to persuade the public to embrace good deeds and names that embody goodness, so as to reject evil and oppose the use of names that carry negative meanings, since African societies believe that a name shapes the character of the individual. An echo is a sound that is repeated after being produced, such as when a person shouts inside a cave or forest, while philosophy refers to the study of the nature, meaning, and reasons for things, as well as wisdom and prudence (Kamusi ya Kiswahili Sanifu, 2013). Therefore, a philosophical echo is a sound that is repeated after being produced through the study of the nature, meaning, and reasons for things, as well as wisdom and prudence. The play "Our Unity, Our Triumph" portrays a woman enduring intense and painful struggles for liberation. The play shows how the woman finds herself on the verge of despair, almost accepting defeat, but with the support of a large community that joins her, she ultimately emerges victorious. This is a philosophical echo that reminds us of the saying that one finger cannot kill a louse and that unity is always victory. According to the Standard Swahili Dictionary (TUKI, 2013), the word “word” is defined as a group of sounds that are spoken or written together to convey meaning. And so, when words are grouped into different units that have not yet reached the status of a clause or a sentence, they are called phrases (Kipacha, 2005). Therefore, a word and another word form a phrase. Likewise, when phrases are brought together, they form clauses. Massamba (2004) defines a clause as "a construction with a subject and a predicate that exists within a main construction." Several clauses combine to form a sentence; and when several sentences are brought together, they form a construction, which then forms a paragraph, and paragraphs in turn produce an essay. A sentence is a self-contained construction that essentially involves an action and an agent (TUKI, 2013). The author has used several symbols intertwined with mythology, particularly African mythologies. One of the symbols that carries a well-known mythology among many African communities and globally is the large black serpent (Dragon). According to Morris (in Shanafelt, 2014), the serpent as a symbol (especially the python) is associated with rain, water, the ecological chain, fertility, and magical/spiritual powers, as well as a sign of death and resurrection. The mythology outlined by this scholar regarding the serpent and its meanings also appears in sacred texts, particularly the Holy Bible (Genesis 3:14-15, Genesis 44:5, Exodus 7:8-12, Numbers 21:6-9, 1 John 3:8, Revelation 12:9, Revelation 12:17, Revelation 20:2,10). This is why the serpent, as a symbol, has great power, stemming from faith-based traditions in the cultures of various societies, not only in Africa but throughout the world (Hambly, 1929; Lynch and Roberts, 2010; Thomas, 2011; Shanafelt, 2014). Moreover, the use of the snake as an artistic symbol is not limited to this play alone but also appears in other Kiswahili creative works. Oral literature, as an ancient art form, often employs large snakes and other creatures to represent God, gods, spirits, humans, or certain concepts through imagery. Therefore, the imagery of creatures such as large snakes is part of the richness carried in traditional narratives, which we also observe in both oral and written traditional literature (Bertoncini, 1989; Madumulla, 2009). Uchambuzi ni mchakato wa kisayansi wa kuchunguza maandiko kwa lengo la kutambua yaliyomo ndani yao, sababu ya uwepo wa kile ambacho kimetambuliwa, jinsi kipengele hicho maalum imejengwa, na maana inayotokana na maandiko maalum, yote kwa kusudi la kutoa ufafanuzi kulingana na vigezo vya wachambuzi. Makala hii inatoa uchambuzi unaolenga kutambua uwepo wa ushirikiano katika mchezo wetu wa ushirikiano na ushindi wa Anitha E. Mgimba. Ikiwa ndivyo, ni ya aina gani? Kwa kuongezea, uchambuzi umeonyesha waziwazi uwepo wa ushirikiano mkubwa ndani ya mchezo huo. Hata hivyo, makala hii inaonyesha tu mambo matano hususa ambayo yamezingatiwa katika mchezo huo uliochaguliwa. Hayo yanatia ndani maandishi ya kidini (maandishi kutoka kwenye vitabu vitakatifu), usemi wa mfano katika kuchagua na kuunda wahusika, sauti za falsafa, majina ya sura au hadithi, na hekaya za alama. Kulingana na kanuni hizi, tunaweza kusema kuwa intertextuality ni nadharia na ujuzi wa kitaaluma ambao huchunguza Nadharia hii ilitoka kwa mawazo ya mazungumzo ya msomi wa Urusi, Mikhail Bakhtin (alizaliwa 1895, alikufa 1975), na baadaye iliboreshwa na mwanasayansi wa Kifaransa, Julia Kristeva (Wamitila, 2002; Wafula na Njogu, 2007). Hapa ni sahihi kusema kwamba Julia Kristeva ni mwanzilishi wa nadharia ya Intertextuality baada ya refining Mikhail Bakhtin  ya nadharia ya Dialogism katika miaka ya 1960. Bakhtin anatuhakikishia kwamba kazi yoyote ya fasihi ina sauti mbalimbali. Ushirikiano huu, kwa maneno mengine, pia huitwa sauti. Watu walioachwa kando; hasa wanawake na watoto. Mchezo huu unathamini athari hizi na kisha huonyesha jinsi uhuru wa kiakili, kitamaduni, na kijamii unapaswa kukuza umoja na ushirikiano ndani ya jamii kubwa ili kuwasaidia walioachwa kando kufikia uhuru wa kibinafsi. Mchezo huu hutumia lugha ambayo inaeleweka haraka na kwa urahisi na mtu yeyote anayejua Kiswahili vizuri. Mazungumzo yaliyojengwa katika mchezo huu huibua mada anuwai kama vile uhuru, jukumu la wanawake katika jamii, tabaka za kijamii, saboto, ubinafsi, njama, ukandamizaji, chuki, wivu, pupa, ulaghai, unyanyasaji, ubaguzi, uwazi na ukweli, mila na mila, umoja na mshikamano, malezi ya familia, juhudi na maendeleo endelevu, umuhimu wa kuhifadhi rekodi na kutambua mali, pamoja na usimamizi na maendeleo ya mali, kati ya zingine. Ni muhimu kwa msomaji wa makala hii kuelewa kwamba intertextuality haiwezi kutambuliwa katika maandishi kama mchambuzi hana ujuzi wa awali au familiarity na maarifa, mbinu, ujuzi, na sifa kupatikana katika maandishi mbalimbali ya awali. Kwa hiyo, mtu ambaye anaweza kutambua intertextuality katika kazi za kisanii lazima kuwa na ujuzi sana na curious binafsi, mtu na kiu na njaa ya maarifa, mbinu, ujuzi, na tabia ya ajabu ya ajabu ya curiousness alipata kwa kuchunguza kazi mbalimbali za ubunifu na mbalimbali ya maandishi kitaaluma. kinyume chake, msomaji haitaweza kutambua intertextuality ndani ya kazi ya ubunifu wanayoisoma kama wao si akili kutambua resonance ya maarifa, mbinu, ujuzi, na sifa kupatikana katika kazi za awali. Mchezo ni tajiri katika majaribio mbalimbali ya kisanii na nadharia na mbinu. Kwa mfano, ndani ya mchezo, kuna intertextuality kwa kuwa kila sura ni kupewa subtopic ambayo inahusu maneno ya lugha kutoka uwanja wa lugha muundo, ili kuonyesha kuzaliwa na maendeleo ya mada ni kujadiliwa na mwandishi. Hadithi za kipagani zilizoelezwa na msomi huyu kuhusu nyoka na maana zake pia zinaonekana katika maandiko matakatifu, hasa Biblia Takatifu (Mwanzo 3:14-15, Mwanzo 44:5, Kutoka 7:8-12, Hesabu 21:6-9, 1 Yohana 3:8, Ufunuo 12:9, Ufunuo 12:17, Ufunuo 20:2,10). Hii ndio sababu nyoka, kama ishara, ana nguvu kubwa, inayotokana na mila ya imani katika tamaduni za jamii anuwai, sio tu barani Afrika lakini ulimwenguni kote (Hambly, 1929; Lynch na Roberts, 2010; Thomas, 2011; Shanafelt, 2014). Si lugha tu inayoonekana kuwa na sauti ndani ya mchezo huu, lakini pia kuna aina nyingine ya sauti. Sauti hii ni kufanana kwa mtindo kati ya *Utangamano Wetu Ushindi Wetu * na maonyesho mengine kadhaa ya Kiswahili, kwa mfano, *Ngoswe Penzi Kitovu cha Uzembe * (1988) na Edwin Semzaba na *Nje  Ndani * (2016) na A. A. Majid Mswahili na M. S. Njonjolo. Edwin Semzaba ametumia ujuzi kutoka kwa taaluma ya Geomorphology kuchagua na kuanzisha njama ili kuonyesha mizizi ya tatizo hadi athari zake. Utambulisho huu umetumia dhana zifuatazo kwa mfuatano: Streamlet  Tribute  River  Channel  Kwa Bahari. Vivyo hivyo, A. A. Majid Mswahili na M. S. Njonjolo wametumia mbinu kutoka katika nyanja za afya na dawa kuchagua na kutambua njama zao ili kuonyesha chanzo cha tatizo hilo hadi athari zake. Walitumia mfululizo wa maonyesho yafuatayo: Trigger ya awali  Dalili ya kwanza (Papule)  Dalili ya pili (Papule)  Dalili ya tatu (Nodule)  Dalili ya nne (Abscess)  Dalili ya tano (Abscesses)  Dalili ya sita (Ulcer). Maelezo haya hutuongoza kutambua kwamba matumizi ya joka, hasa nyoka wa kuogopesha, katika kazi za ubunifu si kitu kipya lakini badala ya kuendelea na mazoezi ya sanaa ya kuchora kutoka utamaduni wa kijamiimasimulizina kuingiza katika kazi mpya za ubunifu. Katika mchezo Utangamano Wetu Ushindi Wetu, mwandishi anaonyesha uhusiano kati ya alama ya nyoka na maana yake kuhusiana na hekaya. Kwa hivyo, mchezo wa Utangamano Wetu Ushindi Wetu unaonyesha ushawishi wa ujuzi wa mawasiliano na taaluma za lugha Morphology na Syntax katika uteuzi na utambuzi wa majina yake ya njama. Kama Morris (katika Shanafelt, 2014) alisema, nguvu za kichawi zinaweza kutumia nyoka kama moja ya alama za uwongo. Uthibitisho wa nyoka akionyesha uwepo wa nguvu za uchawi unapatikana katika nukuu hii: Kupitia nukuu hizi, tunaona kwamba mchezo wa kuigiza *Utangamano Wetu Ushindi Wetu* una mambo ya mfano ya kati ya maandishi yanayoonyesha hekaya za kudumu za Waafrika na pia jamii nyingine nje ya bara la Afrika. Isitoshe, kutumia nyoka kama ishara ya sanaa si tu katika mchezo huu bali pia huonekana katika kazi nyingine za ubunifu za Kiswahili. Uandishi wa mdomo, kama aina ya sanaa ya kale, mara nyingi hutumia nyoka wakubwa na viumbe wengine kuwakilisha Mungu, miungu, roho, wanadamu, au dhana fulani kupitia picha. Kwa hivyo, picha za viumbe kama nyoka wakubwa ni sehemu ya utajiri uliobeba katika hadithi za jadi, ambazo pia tunaona katika fasihi ya jadi ya mdomo na ya maandishi (Bertoncini, 1989; Madumulla, 2009). Baadhi ya kazi za kufikiri zinazoonyesha matumizi ya nyoka mkubwa kwa njia ya mfano na ya maana, ambayo tunaweza kuhusisha na mchezo wa kuigiza *Utangamano Wetu Ushindi Wetu*, ni: *Adili na Ndugu zake* (Robert, 1952), *Mtu Mashuhuri katika Historia ya Usukuma* (Boaz, 1974), *Shield ya jadi* (Hussein, 1976), *Hero Gishegu* (Masatu, hakuna mwaka), *Nondo anayekula binadamu*, *Nunda anayekula binadamu na Hadithi zingine* (Hellier, 1964), *The Dance of Ngamalundi* (Mbogo, 1988), na *The Snakes Skin* (Kezila, 2006). Katika kazi hizi zote, matumizi ya nyoka mkubwa hubeba ishara ya uchawi, mali ya ajabu, kifo, kipengele cha ulinzi, usalama na ulinzi, mateso, mamlaka ya uchawi, ud Kazi hizi ni za zamani kuliko ile drama tuliyochunguza. discourses.source_txt: Intertextuality is a method, skill, or discipline and a guide for the scientific analysis of texts, especially artistic and non-artistic works, to determine the presence of influence through borrowing or dialogue; that is, the similarity in form, content, and technique between one text and another. This resemblance can be direct or involve proximity. Such interaction is also referred to as an echo.
discourses.translated_txt: Intertextuality ni njia, ustadi, au nidhamu na mwongozo kwa ajili ya uchambuzi wa kisayansi wa maandishi, hasa sanaa na kazi zisizo za kisanii, ili kuamua uwepo wa ushawishi kupitia kukopa au mazungumzo; yaani, kufanana kwa fomu, maudhui, na mbinu kati ya maandishi moja na nyingine. Ukweli huu unaweza kuwa moja kwa moja au kuhusisha ukaribu.

discourses.source_txt: It is believed that intertextuality is among the oldest compositional techniques; however, as a critical approach, it still appears to be unfamiliar and has not been extensively addressed in the field of Kiswahili literature and art. For this reason, this article will contribute to the Kiswahili body of work dealing with criticism through the theory of intertextuality, in order to identify the intertextuality present in texts, for example in the play Our Cohesion Our Triumph.
discourses.translated_txt: Inaaminika kuwa intertextuality ni miongoni mwa mbinu za zamani zaidi za utungaji; hata hivyo, kama mbinu muhimu, bado inaonekana kuwa haijulikani na haijazungumziwa sana katika uwanja wa fasihi na sanaa ya Kiswahili. Kwa sababu hii, nakala hii itachangia kazi ya Kiswahili inayoshughulikia ukosoaji kupitia nadharia ya intertextuality, ili kutambua intertextuality iliyopo katika maandishi, kwa mfano katika mchezo wetu wa ushirikiano wetu Ushindi wetu.

discourses.source_txt: The results of the analysis have revealed a considerable presence of intertextuality connected to the author’s upbringing and development in religious (spiritual), physical (cultural and moral), social, and academic dimensions – in one way or another. It is part of these findings that constitutes this article.
discourses.translated_txt: Matokeo ya uchambuzi wa imeonyesha uwepo mkubwa wa intertextuality kuhusiana na elimu na maendeleo ya mwandishi katika dini (roho), kimwili (kitamaduni na kimaadili), kijamii, na elimu vipimo  kwa njia moja au nyingine. Ni sehemu ya matokeo haya ambayo ni makala hii.

discourses.source_txt: Therefore, this article presents the intertextuality between the selected play Our Cohesion Our Triumph and writings from sacred books, allegory in the selection and creation of characters, philosophical echoes, chapter or plot titles, and the mythology of symbols.
discourses.translated_txt: Kwa hiyo, makala hii inaonyesha jinsi ambavyo mchezo wetu wa kuigiza, Our Cohesion Our Triumph, unavyohusiana na maandishi ya vitabu vitakatifu, mifano ya kuchagua na kuunda wahusika, maneno ya kifalsafa, sura au hadithi za hadithi, na hekaya za alama.

THEORETICAL FRAMEWORK  
These principles are: (i) it is not easy and indeed impossible to view a text as a product that is an orphan, in its own uniqueness and in isolation; instead, we must recognize that there are preceding texts that are related to the new text; (ii) texts interact and influence each other, so to think that a literary text is self-sufficient and independent is willful blindness; and (iii) an artistic text invites certain modes of expression and specific codes which help to signal an idea, event, work, or another subsequent work—thereby creating an impact on the creative work that follows (Kristeva, 1980). Based on these principles, we can say that intertextuality is a theory and academic skill that examines, identifies, and explains the relationships that exist between one text and another, in order to determine the direct or indirect (echoed) effects resulting from the interactions and mutual reinforcement of these texts. In other words, the theory of intertextuality is a guide for analyzing works of art, with a focus on literary texts, to determine the existence of borrowing or dialogue; that is, resemblance in genre, theme, and technique between one text and another. discourses.source_txt: What is important for the reader of this article to understand is that intertextuality cannot be identified in a text if the analyst lacks background knowledge or familiarity with the knowledge, techniques, skills, and traits found in various preceding texts. Therefore, a person who can identify intertextuality in artistic works must be a highly knowledgeable and inquisitive individual, someone with a thirst and hunger for knowledge, techniques, skills, and the characteristic curiosity gained through exploring various creative works and a range of academic writings. On the contrary, a reader will not be able to discern the intertextuality within the creative work they are reading if they do not mentally perceive the resonances of knowledge, techniques, skills, and traits found in earlier works.

discourses.source_txt: This reason is consistent with what is thoroughly explained by Taylor and Taylor (1983) in their well-known book The Psychology of Reading. discourses.source_txt: This is irrefutable evidence that the ideas and foundations of Mikhail Bakhtin and Julia Kristeva are not merely speculative but are concrete and scientifically valid, because (i) it is neither easy nor possible to regard a text as a unique product, in its singularity and in isolation; instead, there must be preceding texts related to the new text; (ii) texts interact and influence each other, therefore to think that a literary text is self-sufficient and independent is erroneous; (iii) an artistic text invites certain stylistic forms of expression and particular codes that help signify an idea, event, work, or subsequent works.
discourses.translated_txt: Hii ni ushahidi usioweza kupingwa kwamba mawazo na misingi ya Mikhail Bakhtin na Julia Kristeva sio tu ya utabiri lakini ni halisi na ya kisayansi halali, kwa sababu (i) ni rahisi wala haiwezekani kuona maandishi kama bidhaa ya kipekee, katika kipekee chake na kwa kujitenga; badala yake, lazima kuwe na maandishi ya awali yanayohusiana na maandishi mapya; (ii) maandishi yanaingiliana na kuathiri kila mmoja, kwa hivyo kufikiri kwamba maandishi ya fasihi ni yenye kujitosheleza na huru ni kosa; (iii) maandishi ya kisanii hualika aina fulani za usemi na kanuni maalum ambazo husaidia kutambulisha wazo, tukio, kazi, au kazi za baadaye.

This table shows the quotations we identified from the play "Utangamano Wetu Ushindi Wetu" that are similar or correspond to quotations from the Holy Bible.
discourses.translated_txt: Metaphor in the Selection and Creation of Characters Jedwali hili linaonyesha nukuu ambazo tumetambua kutoka kwa drama "Utangamano Wetu Ushindi Wetu" ambazo ni sawa au zinafanana na nukuu kutoka Biblia Takatifu.

discourses.source_txt: This is indisputable evidence that this play was not created out of thin air, but rather the writer drew knowledge, skills, and experience from the sacred writings of the religion that raised and nurtured him, as we noted in the writer’s biography. All the quotations we referenced clearly reflect the echoes of earlier texts, thus strongly confirming that composition and writing cannot be divorced from the influence of preceding texts or the physical and spiritual environments that raised and shaped the writer.
discourses.translated_txt: Hii ni ushahidi usioweza kupingwa kwamba mchezo huu haukuundwa nje ya hewa, lakini badala ya mwandishi alichukua maarifa, ujuzi, na uzoefu kutoka kwa maandishi matakatifu ya dini ambayo ilimlea na kumlea, kama tulivyoona katika wasifu wa mwandishi.

discourses.source_txt: That is why Worton and Still (1990) emphasize that every text is a supplement to another text.

discourses.source_txt: There is no text that is complete and does not require supplementation from other texts in order to be meaningful and comprehensible. This means that no text functions as a closed, self-contained system; rather, every text is dependent on preceding texts.

discourses.source_txt: Allegory is an artistic device used by a writer to choose a name that reflects the character, behavior, and experiences of a character in the work they are creating. For example, a writer may name their character “Hasidi” (The Envious One). To justify this name, the writer must develop that character to act with envy from beginning to end. The selection and creation of characters whose traits align with their names is the artistic technique known as allegory.
discourses.translated_txt: Allegory ni kifaa cha sanaa ambacho mwandishi hutumia kuchagua jina ambalo linaonyesha tabia, tabia, na uzoefu wa tabia katika kazi wanayounda. Kwa mfano, mwandishi anaweza kumwita tabia yake Hasidi (Mchukizo). Ili kuhalalisha jina hili, mwandishi lazima avute tabia hiyo kutenda kwa wivu kutoka mwanzo hadi mwisho. Uchaguzi na uundaji wa wahusika ambao sifa zao zinaambatana na majina yao ni mbinu ya kisanii inayojulikana kama allegory.

discourses.source_txt: Normally, these characters possess the traits of flat characters (those who do not undergo changes in character) in order to justify their names, because if they were to change in character, their names would no longer correspond to their new traits. Therefore, in terms of character and stance, these characters remain unchanged from the beginning to the end of the play. Mlacha and Madumulla (1991) describe such characters as ones who do not appear to grow in character, actions, or psychologically.
discourses.translated_txt: Kwa kawaida, wahusika hawa wana sifa za wahusika wa gorofa (wale ambao hawapati mabadiliko ya tabia) ili kuhalalisha majina yao, kwa sababu ikiwa wangebadilisha tabia, majina yao hayangefaa tena sifa zao mpya. Kwa hivyo, kwa suala la tabia na msimamo, wahusika hawa hubaki bila kubadilika kutoka mwanzo hadi mwisho wa mchezo. Mlacha na Madumulla (1991) wanaelezea wahusika kama wale ambao hawaonekani kukua kwa tabia, vitendo, au kisaikolojia.

Philosophical and Conceptual Echo

An echo is a sound that is repeated after being produced, such as when a person shouts inside a cave or forest, while philosophy refers to the study of the nature, meaning, and reasons for things, as well as wisdom and prudence (Kamusi ya Kiswahili Sanifu, 2013). discourses.source_txt: The title serves as the identifier of the chapter or scenes within a written play. The play *Utangamano Wetu Ushindi Wetu* appears to organize its plot using two types of titles – main and sub-titles.

discourses.source_txt: The main titles (and sub-titles in brackets) used are: Part One (Word), Part Two (Phrase), Part Three (Clauses), Part Four (Sentence), Part Five (Composition), Part Six (Paragraph), and Part Seven (Essay). When we look at the words used as sub-titles to identify the plot, we find that these words are derived from the field of Linguistics – Morphology and Syntax as described and discussed in Massamba, Kihore, and Hokororo (2012), as well as in the field of communication skills.
discourses.translated_txt: Majina kuu (na vichwa vya habari chini katika brackets) kutumika ni: Sehemu ya Kwanza (Neno), Sehemu ya Pili (Frases), Sehemu ya Tatu (Clausles), Sehemu ya Nne (Sentence), Sehemu ya Tano (Composition), Sehemu ya Sita (Paragrafu), na Sehemu ya Saba (Essay). Tunapoangalia maneno kutumika kama vichwa vya habari kutambua njama, tunagundua kuwa maneno haya yanatokana na uwanja wa Linguistics  Morphology na Syntax kama ilivyoelezwa na kuzungumziwa katika Massamba, Kihore, and Hokororo (2012), pamoja na katika uwanja wa ujuzi wa mawasiliano.

discourses.source_txt: These words are not just mere words but academic concepts that refer to fundamental elements in these two disciplines.
